overview: Number Representation 4 skills test karta hai: base/radix conversion (aur unknown-radix equations), two's complement representation aur range, overflow detection (arithmetic ke baad), aur bit-counting/special numeric properties (floating point included).
whyItMatters: 57 PYQs — poore corpus ka 2nd highest-PYQ topic. Ye 'quick, mechanical, high-accuracy' topic hai — formulas clear hone ke baad bahut fast solve hota hai.
coreConcept: Kisi bhi base-b number ko decimal me convert karne ka formula: digit × b^position, sum karo. Two's complement negative numbers represent karne ka standard tarika hai: invert all bits, add 1. Overflow tab hota hai jab result ki magnitude representable range se BAHAR chali jaaye (sirf SAME-SIGN operands add karne par possible — do opposite-sign numbers add karne se overflow KABHI nahi hota).
hinglishExplanation: Base conversion ko ek 'counting system translation' socho — jaise Hindi se English translate karna, bas yahan numbers translate ho rahe hain ek 'counting base' se doosre me. Two's complement ka trick yaad rakho: 'sabko ulta karo (invert), phir 1 jod do' — negative number turant mil jaata hai. Overflow sirf tab hota hai jab DONO operands SAME sign ke hon (dono positive ya dono negative) aur result ki sign GALAT aa jaaye — do OPPOSITE sign wale numbers add karne se overflow kabhi possible hi nahi hai (result hamesha range ke andar rahega).
formalDefinition: Base-b number d_n...d_1d_0 = Σ d_i × b^i. Two's complement of an n-bit number x: invert all bits, add 1 (equivalently, 2^n - x for x≠0).
importantProperties: n-bit two's complement range: -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1)-1 (one extra negative value compared to positive — asymmetric range, a classic trap).
n-bit sign-magnitude / 1's complement range: -(2^(n-1)-1) to 2^(n-1)-1 (SYMMETRIC, but has TWO representations of zero: +0 and -0).
Two's complement has EXACTLY ONE representation of zero (no +0/-0 distinction) — a key advantage over sign-magnitude/1's complement.

Overflow in addition (two's complement): occurs IFF the carry INTO the sign bit ≠ the carry OUT of the sign bit (the 'carry mismatch' rule) — equivalently, occurs only when adding two SAME-sign numbers and the result has the OPPOSITE sign.
Adding a POSITIVE and a NEGATIVE number (opposite signs) can NEVER cause overflow — the true result is always within range.
Sign extension: to extend a signed number to more bits, REPLICATE the sign bit (not just pad with 0s) — padding with 0s only works for extending UNSIGNED/POSITIVE numbers correctly.

For unknown-radix equations (like '44 in base x = 32 in base y'), set up the polynomial equation directly and solve algebraically — often has MULTIPLE valid (x,y) solutions, count them all when asked.

formulas.baseToDecimal: Σ (digit_i × base^i), summed over all digit positions
formulas.signMagnitudeRange: n-bit sign-magnitude/1's complement: -(2^(n-1)-1) to 2^(n-1)-1, with two zero representations
formulas.overflowRule: Overflow ⟺ (carry into sign bit) ≠ (carry out of sign bit); equivalently, only possible when adding SAME-sign operands and result sign flips
formulas.twosComplementOfX: Two's complement of x (n bits) = 2^n - x (for x≠0), or equivalently invert-all-bits-then-add-1

keyPropertiesAndIdentities: The two's complement range asymmetry (one more negative value than positive) comes from the fact that the all-1s pattern (representing -2^(n-1)) has no positive counterpart in the same n bits.
For MULTIPLICATION of two n-bit two's complement numbers, the product needs UP TO 2n bits to represent without overflow (not just n bits) — a common bit-width-sizing question.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting the two's complement range is ASYMMETRIC (more negative numbers than positive) — off-by-one errors on the boundary values are extremely common.
Confusing the overflow rule with 'any carry out of the MSB means overflow' — the correct rule needs BOTH the carry-in and carry-out of the sign bit position, comparing them.
Padding with 0s instead of sign-extending when widening a NEGATIVE two's complement number — must replicate the sign bit.
Assuming opposite-sign addition can overflow — it mathematically cannot in two's complement.
Missing that sign-magnitude/1's complement has TWO zero representations while two's complement has only ONE — affects range/count calculations.
standardTechniques: For base conversion: apply the positional-value formula directly (multiply each digit by base^position, sum).

For unknown-radix equations: set up algebraic equations from the positional formula, solve for the unknown base(s) — check ALL valid solutions (base must be a positive integer greater than the largest digit used).
For overflow detection: compute the actual sum in two's complement, check the sign-bit-carry-in vs carry-out condition directly (don't just eyeball the result).
For range questions: apply the exact asymmetric formula for two's complement, don't assume symmetry.
